events.label: US import bans on Canadian dairy, motorcycles and alcoholic beverages take effect
events.note: Follows Canada's 15%-50% retaliatory tariffs on ~$20B of US goods (Sept 8) and the removal of Canadian-origin products from federal schedules worth $50B+ a year. A cost-push input running alongside $100 crude.

events.label: Seven-day window closes on the reported Iranian offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
events.note: Updated Sep 22 night: Saudi Arabia restarted the East-West pipeline (about 4m b/d, ~4% of global supply), so the bypass around the strait is open again and the market no longer needs Hormuz reopened to get the barrels. The window now tests whether the strait itself reopens on the reported timetable or the pipeline restart is the only supply that returned. Brent reclaiming $100 says the restart is slower than priced; under $95 says the barrels are treated as back. Updated Sep 23 morning: Reuters reported a senior Iranian official putting terms on the offer — an easing of military pressure and the lifting of the port blockade — and said the proposal reached Washington through mediators on Sep 16. Trump told the UN he expects a deal only after the November midterms, so the window and the administration's stated timeline are roughly seven weeks apart. Updated Sep 23 night: Pezeshkian said the Islamic Republic would not surrender and Brent reversed 3.9% to $103.08, recovering roughly half the decline from the $108 Sep 14 high. The window now tests a stated refusal as well as a reported offer. Updated Sep 25 morning: Foreign Minister Araghchi put the offer on the record as a seven-day plan whose clock starts only when Washington accepts Tehran's conditions — release of at least $12 billion in frozen assets, a waiver on Iranian oil sanctions and the end of the naval blockade. Sep 29 is therefore the end of the reported window, not a deadline either side has accepted; a US acceptance would start a new seven-day clock.

events.label: Micron fiscal Q4 — consensus near $50.8bn revenue and $31.43 adjusted EPS, the first hard AI-capex number since the long end repriced
events.note: Added Sep 23 night: Micron rose 5.00% to $1,096.16 on a session the Nasdaq fell 1.13% and the thirty-year closed at its highest since 2004, so the name diverged from both the index and the discount rate. Memory pricing is the one AI-capex line that reports before the quarter ends, which makes this the print that either validates the divergence or closes it. It also lands on quarter end.

events.label: AMD's reported ~10% price increase on AI accelerators, Radeon GPUs and chipsets takes effect (Q4 start) — unconfirmed by the company
events.note: Added Sep 18 morning: AMD notified partners on Sep 17 of a roughly 10% increase from the fourth quarter, citing higher TSMC wafer costs, with Ryzen CPUs left off the list. TSMC is separately reported to have told Nvidia, Apple, AMD and Qualcomm of 5%–10% wafer increases, 8%–10% on sub-5nm. If it holds, it is the first broad pass-through of foundry cost into AI hardware pricing and a gross-margin question for every fabless buyer, not just AMD. A company denial takes it back. Updated Sep 21 night: this increase is now the only committed commercial number behind the Sep 21 CPU re-rating that carried AMD to a record $613.31 and briefly past $1 trillion in market value. It is effective Oct 1 but does not appear in a reported result until AMD's late-October print, which is the first hard test of the thesis.

events.label: Nike fiscal Q1 — the tariff and China-demand channel, reporting a week later than the calendar carried it
events.note: Added Sep 23 night: the date was previously carried as Sep 24 and is Oct 1. Nike is the check on whether the tariff and Chinese-demand problem Volkswagen described in September is a European luxury issue or a broader one, and it lands the same day AMD's reported ~10% accelerator price increase takes effect.

events.label: Third-quarter bank earnings open - the test of whether Sep 16's regional selloff was deposit betas or positioning
events.note: Added Sep 16 night: on the day of the hike the SPDR S&P Bank ETF fell 2.6%, its worst session since February 27, with Huntington Bancshares down 5.6% and Citizens Financial 4.8% against JPMorgan's roughly 1%. A four-to-five-times gap between regional and money-center names prices deposit competition and credit at a 4.1% funds rate held through 2027, not net interest margin. Mid-October results either show that in deposit betas and provisions or they do not. The date is indicative of the usual opening week.

events.label: Anthropic IPO roadshow opens (indicative) — potentially the largest listing in history at up to $2T, days ahead of the November midterms
events.note: Added Sep 14 night: the date is indicative, not scheduled — the timeline moved from September to mid-October at the earliest. A $2 trillion debut would eclipse SpaceX's $1.77 trillion June 2026 listing. The supply side of the AI trade absorbing an offering that size, into a long end that touched 5% on the ten-year in September, is the test no earnings print delivers.

events.label: Saudi East-West pipeline returns to full capacity (approx.) - Aramco targets full capability on the 7 million b/d line roughly six weeks from Sep 16, after restoring about half within days via a bypass
events.note: Updated Sep 22 night: the line restarted Sep 22 after being shut since the Sep 13 drone attacks, with Yanbu exports resuming. One security source briefed on the work said complete resumption could take weeks against Aramco's aim of restoring full capability quickly.

events.label: October FOMC decision (indicative date) - hike odds about 76% on CME FedWatch, so the skip case is now the minority view
events.note: Added Sep 16 night: the date is indicative pending the published Fed table. Market pricing entered Sep 16 charging roughly 41 bp of total 2026 tightening including that day's 25 bp; the September projections imply another full quarter point this year and no easing through 2027, and 16 of 18 officials see at least one more increase. October pricing moved to roughly 50% by the close. A ten-year back under 4.94% with October odds falling toward 25% would say the press-conference repricing was a one-session reaction; a hold above 5.04% would say the market has accepted 4.1% held for five more quarters. Updated Sep 17 morning: Goldman Sachs noted the Fed will likely skip October given its proximity to the Nov 3 midterms, which makes December the next live meeting and gives the market eleven weeks of inflation and labour data to argue with the dots rather than five. The CNBC Fed Survey has 55% of respondents expecting more than a single further hike. A longer runway cuts both ways - eleven weeks of falling crude would discount the dots as readily as eleven weeks of pass-through would confirm them. Updated Sep 23 night: the flash PMI at 58.4 and Barr saying the committee was "out of position" and that "further policy adjustments are likely to be needed" took October odds to about 73% from roughly 60% held through the whole crude decline. The skip case now has to argue against an activity survey as well as the dots. Updated Sep 25 morning: Williams called another increase by year-end 'reasonable' on Sep 24 and FedWatch reached about 77.5%; it eased to about 71% on Sep 25 as oil and yields fell back on Iran's public Hormuz offer. Pricing is moving with oil more than with Fed speakers.

events.label: US midterm elections — Trump's pledged $5,000 per-adult 'dividend' is contingent on Republicans holding both chambers
events.note: Pointed at about $154.5B of tariff revenue in the first ten months of FY2026; even 100 million recipients would cost $500B. The House is currently projected to go to the Democrats, so it is a tail input — but it lands on a long end that spent September repricing term premium.

events.label: Treasury expanded long-end buyback program ends — ops of at least $4B run from September 9
events.note: The count of completed operations is what separates absorbed supply from purchased calm at the long end. Updated Sep 10 night: the 30Y cleared 5.33%, August 18's prior high, and closed at 5.37% — its highest since 2007 — while the program was buying that maturity. The 2007 peak is 5.44%. Updated Sep 23 night: the thirty-year closed at 5.40%, the highest close since 2004 and four basis points under the 5.44% 2007 peak, while the program is still bidding that maturity — the buyback is now the clearest read on whether the long end is absorbing supply or being held.

events.label: China's suspension of rare-earth export controls expires on its original date — the tariff truce itself was extended to January 10 (Bessent, Sep 23)
events.note: The trade deadline moved out of the quarter; whether the rare-earth suspension moves with it is the open question for the chip supply chain

events.label: Grand Theft Auto VI release date — the scheduled window Take-Two's 17% 2026 decline is pricing scepticism about
events.note: Added Sep 17 morning: Take-Two held its annual shareholder meeting on Sep 17 with the title still scheduled for Nov 19 after repeated delays. The stock is down 17% in 2026, so the market is discounting the date rather than the title. A reaffirmation or a further slip is what revalues it, and the release lands sixteen days after the midterms and three weeks before the December FOMC.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — terminal insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut. Lock-up expiries are the known supply overhang for hot IPOs. Context after Aug 6-7: 20% first tranche absorbed at $105-$115; next tranches scheduled Aug 20 and late September. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October call) is the only fundamental catalyst that could revalue the lockup discount before the December terminal release. SPCX Q2: $18.37B capex vs $7.81B revenue; AI segment $2.56B (+247% YoY).

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). PLTR's 149% US commercial growth, AMD's $6.7B data-center (+107%), and SpaceX's exclusive Nvidia commitment ($15.83B AI capex) confirm the enterprise AI adoption underlying OpenAI's revenue model. NVDA circular financing disclosure ($250B OpenAI backstop) remains the unresolved structural question that may surface in S-1 filings.

events.label: Extended US-China 'Busan' trade truce expires — Bessent says a larger package or another roll-over are both possible
events.note: Replaces the November deadline as the date the China policy track resolves
